agent: pathfind-signatures: the two member functions whose signature never mentions their class, and the unsigned CPathFind family
question: Whether CPathFind::StepCost (0x1A2A00) really belongs to CPathFind and where its receiver is, whether CParseContext::FreeMessages (0x67BAF0) is a static member or has a receiver in a register, and a signature for every CPathFind-family virtual project.json left unsigned.

addresses.name: CPathFind::Find
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CPathFind::Find(CPathFind* finder, CUnit* unit, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, CList* path)
addresses.comment:
The A* search itself, and **not a member call**: the finder is the first stack argument, not a receiver. The call site at rva 0x1D8F08 pushes five and adds nothing back (the body does `ret 0x14`), and ECX there holds the unit's own province from CUnit +0x130 - so nothing puts the finder in a register.

What it does: refuses unless unit, from and to are all non-null, then asks the finder's slot 1 (MayUse) whether it may run at all. It allocates three arrays the size of the game state's province vector - a visited byte per province, a 16-byte open-list record per province and a came-from index per province - and loops: take the cheapest open province, ask slot 3 (IsGoal), and for each edge of its template (CProvince +0xD4) ask slot 2 (MayStep) and then slot 0 (StepCost). The heuristic added on top is the straight-line distance between the two templates' +0x2C/+0x30 coordinates, wrapped at the map width in CMap +0x2A74 and scaled by [0x1688618]. On success rva 0x1A11F0 fills `path` with 16-byte nodes holding province **ids** (the CList head is first/last/count/flag, the nodes are data/prev/next/flag).
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature at all. Added one: __stdcall with the finder as an ordinary first stack argument, which the call site at 0x1D8F08 settles - five pushes, no caller cleanup against `ret 0x14`, and ECX holding a province rather than the finder. The comment now says what the body does. Wrong if a caller is found that puts the finder in ECX and pushes only four, or if the ret ever reads other than 0x14.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A12B0..0x5A1620 and the call site at 0x5D8EFB-0x5D8F0D. Argument roles read off that site and off the body: arg2 is marked visited and seeded into the open list (0x5A1369-0x5A1381), arg3 is the one the coordinate heuristic measures against (0x5A147B), arg4 is the list rva 0x1A11F0 fills (0x5A15A0). Would be shown wrong by any caller that cleans the stack itself, or by a use of arg2/arg3 that contradicts start/goal.

addresses.name: CPathFind::StepCost
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CPathFind::StepCost(CPathFind* this, CFixedPoint* out, CProvinceTemplate* from, int edge, CMap* map, CUnit* unit)
addresses.comment:
CPathFind slot 0: the cost of stepping out of `from` along its edge number `edge`. **The name is right and the receiver is in ECX.** The body belongs to CPathFind - vtable.py --holding puts it at slot 0 of CPathFind, CSafePathFind, CVerySafePathFind and CPlannedPathFind, which inherit it, while CSafeNavalPathFind overrides it at 0x1A2E00 - and CPathFind::Find loads ECX with the finder at every one of its four dispatch sites (0x1A12E5, 0x1A1390, 0x1A143A, 0x1A145C). The body never reads ECX because these finders are four-byte objects holding nothing but a vftable pointer; that is a `this` that is not needed, not a missing argument. `ret 0x14` accounts for the five stack arguments exactly.

The cost is `from->edges_begin[edge].distance`, in thousandths. Then, if the country controlling `map->provinces[from->edges_begin[edge].to_province]` is hostile to the unit's owner - the tag test at rva 0x2F1B0 - it is scaled by 1100/1000, or by 2000/1000 when that province's intel byte for the owner (CProvince +0x370, bounds-checked against +0x374) is 2 or more **and** units are standing in it (+0x2C0). The two constants are the floats at 0x160A5F0 (1100.5) and 0x160A5F4 (2000.5), truncated to int. Returns `out` in EAX, MSVC's struct return.
addresses.revises: The recorded signature was `void __stdcall StepCost(...)` - no class, no receiver, which is why checkSignatures.py reported it as a member function whose signature never mentions its class. The parameters were right; what was missing is that `this` travels in ECX (the caller sets it) and that the function answers `out` in EAX. Wrong if a dispatch site is found that does not put the finder in ECX, or if the body is ever seen reading ECX before 0x5A2A09 overwrites it.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A2A00..0x5A2AD3; the dispatch at 0x5A145C (`mov ecx,[ebp+8]; mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax]`, five pushes, no cleanup after the call); CSafeNavalPathFind::StepCost at 0x5A2E30-0x5A2E35 forwarding the same five in order and setting no ECX; vtable.py --holding 0x5A2A00. Argument types: arg1 is dereferenced at +0x90 with a 20-byte stride, which is CProvinceTemplate::edges_begin; arg3 at +0x2200 is CMap::provinces and the caller passes g_CMap; arg4 has +0x124/+0x128, CUnit::owner. Shown wrong by a caller passing something other than g_CMap as arg3, or a fourth argument without a CCountryTag at +0x124.

addresses.name: CPathFind::MayUse
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPathFind::MayUse(CPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* from, CProvince* to)
addresses.comment:
CPathFind slot 1: whether this finder may be used for this unit at all. CPathFind::Find asks it once, before allocating anything, and answers false when it does. `this` is not read - see CPathFind::StepCost for why the convention is still __thiscall - and `ret 0xC` covers the three stack arguments.

False unless the unit's own slot 34 (vftable +0x88) accepts `to`. If the unit's slot 16 (+0x40) then says nothing, true; if it does, the test at rva 0xA7D70 - `to` in ECX, `from` in EAX, `&unit->owner` pushed - has to agree as well.
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature at all. Added: __thiscall with `this` in ECX and three stack arguments, matching `ret 0xC`. Wrong if the dispatch at 0x5A12E5 is read as passing four, or if arg1/arg2 turn out not to be the search's from and to.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A25B0..0x5A25FB; the dispatch at 0x5A12DA-0x5A12E5, which pushes Find's arguments 3, 2, 1 in that order with ECX = Find's argument 0. Would be shown wrong by a second call site that passes a different number of arguments.

addresses.name: CPathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPathFind::MayStep(CPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment:
CPathFind slot 2: whether `unit` may step from `from` to `to` along `edge`, with `goal` the search's destination (which the base ignores and both safe finders use). `this` is not read; `ret 0x14` covers the five stack arguments.

Refuses when the edge's kind is 3, when `from` is `to`, when `goal`'s template flag +0x13D is clear, and when the helper at rva 0x1A2600 says a kind-1 edge is blocked - that one reads the province the edge crosses (edge +8) and refuses if its controller is hostile or a foreign unit that is not retreating stands in it. Then the two provinces' templates have to agree: the byte at template **+0x22, unnamed**, may not be set on both, and where it is set on one, that template's **+0xA4, unnamed**, must be the other province's id. What follows is the supply gate: with the destination's controller hostile (rva 0x2F1B0) it refuses a unit whose supply_received_percentage is zero and whose CUnit::SupplyConsumption is positive, and likewise fuel_received_percentage against CUnit::FuelConsumption; and last, the unit owner's relation record for `from`'s controller (country +0xE28 indexed by tag id, byte **+0x4C unnamed**) together with **+0x20** on the record for `to`'s controller refuses the step.
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature at all. Added: __thiscall with `this` in ECX and five stack arguments, matching `ret 0x14`. Wrong if the dispatch at 0x5A143A is read as passing other than five, or if arg1 is not the search goal.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A2700..0x5A29EA and cfg over the same range; the dispatch at 0x5A1424-0x5A143A, whose five pushes are (edge record, neighbour province, current province, Find's `to`, Find's `unit`) - so arg1 is the goal. Corroborated by the two overrides, which return true when arg1 == arg3 (0x5A2B14 and 0x5A2C69): that is the exemption for the last step into the destination and only makes sense if arg1 is the goal and arg3 the candidate. Shown wrong by a call site passing a different count, or by an override that compares arg1 with something else.

addresses.name: CPathFind::IsGoal
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPathFind::IsGoal(CPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* at)
addresses.comment: CPathFind slot 3, which no class in the family overrides: `sete` on `goal == at`, three stack arguments, `ret 0xC`, and neither `this` nor `unit` read. CPathFind::Find asks it for every province it takes off the open list and builds the path the moment it answers 1 (0x5A13B3-0x5A13B7), which is what the name says. Slot 3 was previously recorded only as "unknown" on the CPathFind vftable entry.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A29F0..0x5A29FD (seven instructions) and the dispatch at 0x5A1390-0x5A13B7, where `cmp al,1; je` goes straight to the path reconstruction at 0x5A15A0. vtable.py --holding 0x5A29F0 puts it at slot 3 of all five tables, so it is the base's body and nobody overrides it. The **signature** is confirmed; the **name** is the reading of that one call site, and would be shown wrong by another caller that uses the answer for something other than terminating the search.

addresses.name: CSafePathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CSafePathFind::MayStep(CSafePathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment: CSafePathFind slot 2. Forwards all five arguments unchanged to CPathFind::MayStep (0x5A2AFB-0x5A2B00, no ECX set, callee cleans) and refuses on top of it. Allows the step outright when `to` is the goal - the last step into the destination is exempt. Otherwise it weighs the destination: when the unit's slot 16 or 17 answers true it takes rva 0x1D6900 over `to`'s unit list with the unit's owner tag and multiplies by 1000; when neither does it walks that list itself and adds rva 0x1C3120's value for each unit there whose owner is hostile (rva 0x2F1B0), skipping a `REB` owner when the province's owner tag id (CProvince +0x330) is the unit's own. Either way it refuses when that total is greater than the sum of +0x5C over the unit's own list at CUnit +0xB8.
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature at all. Added: the same shape as the base it forwards to, __thiscall with five stack arguments and `ret 0x14`. Wrong if the forwarding at 0x5A2AFB is read as reordering the arguments.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A2AE0..0x5A2C30. The five pushes at 0x5A2AFB-0x5A2AFF are [ebp+0x18], [ebp+0x14], [ebp+0x10], [ebp+0xC], [ebp+8] in that order, so the base receives them in the same order, and no `add esp` follows the call. vtable.py --holding puts the body in CSafePathFind's table alone. Shown wrong by any use of an argument that contradicts the base's roles.

addresses.name: CVerySafePathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CVerySafePathFind::MayStep(CVerySafePathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment: CVerySafePathFind slot 2, the same shape as CSafePathFind's: forwards all five arguments to CPathFind::MayStep (0x5A2C5B-0x5A2C60), exempts the last step into the goal, and refuses otherwise. It differs in what it does when the unit's slot 16 and slot 17 both say nothing - where the safe one still weighs the units in the destination, this one refuses as soon as the destination's controller is hostile (rva 0x2F1B0) or rva 0xA6010 objects to the province. When either slot does answer it compares rva 0x1D6900 over the destination's unit list (x1000) against the sum of +0x5C over CUnit +0xB8, exactly as the safe one does.
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature at all. Added: the same shape as the base it forwards to, __thiscall with five stack arguments and `ret 0x14`. Wrong if the forwarding at 0x5A2C5B is read as reordering the arguments.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A2C40..0x5A2D18. The five pushes at 0x5A2C5B-0x5A2C5F are [ebp+0x18], [ebp+0x14], [ebp+0x10], [ebp+0xC], [ebp+8], no cleanup after the call, `ret 0x14` on both exits. The goal exemption is the `cmp edi,ebx; je` at 0x5A2C69, arg1 against arg3. Shown wrong by an argument use that contradicts the base's roles.

addresses.name: CPlannedPathFind::MayUse
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPlannedPathFind::MayUse(CPlannedPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* from, CProvince* to)
addresses.comment: CPlannedPathFind slot 1, two instructions: `mov al,1; ret 0xC`. It always allows the finder to run, whatever the unit and the two provinces are, which is what a planning finder wants - the base refuses outright for units whose slot 34 turns the destination down. The body is in CPlannedPathFind's table only, so it is not one the linker folded.
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature at all. Added: the same shape as the CPathFind::MayUse it overrides, __thiscall with three stack arguments, which `ret 0xC` confirms. Wrong only if the base's own argument list is wrong, since this body reads none of them.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A2D20 (`mov al,1; ret 0xC`), and vtable.py --holding 0x5A2D20, which finds it in one table - so the folded-body rule does not apply. The argument list is taken from the slot it overrides, CPathFind::MayUse at 0x1A25B0, whose own list is settled at the dispatch site; this body reads nothing, so the only check available here is the `ret`.

addresses.name: CPlannedPathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPlannedPathFind::MayStep(CPlannedPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment: CPlannedPathFind slot 2, and the only override that does **not** call the base. It keeps the base's first tests and drops everything after them: refuses a kind-3 edge and `from == to`, applies the same template rule (the byte at template +0x22 may not be set on both, and where it is set on one, that template's +0xA4 must be the other province's id), and asks the unit's slot 16 (+0x40), slot 15 (+0x3C) and slot 34 (+0x88, with `to`). No supply, fuel, intel or relation test - a plan is drawn without them.
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature at all. Added: the same shape as the CPathFind::MayStep it overrides, __thiscall with five stack arguments and `ret 0x14`. Wrong if its argument uses contradict the base's - they do not: [ebp+0x18] is the edge (`cmp [eax],3` at 0x5A2D36, as at 0x5A270C) and [ebp+0x10]/[ebp+0x14] are the two provinces it compares.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A2D30..0x5A2DFD, every exit `ret 0x14`. vtable.py --holding 0x5A2D30 finds one table. Shown wrong by a use of [ebp+0xC] - which this body never reads - that contradicted `goal`.

addresses.name: CSafeNavalPathFind::StepCost
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CSafeNavalPathFind::StepCost(CSafeNavalPathFind* this, CFixedPoint* out, CProvinceTemplate* from, int edge, CMap* map, CUnit* unit)
addresses.comment: CSafeNavalPathFind slot 0: the base cost, then a multiplier for what is on the shore. Forwards all five arguments to CPathFind::StepCost (0x5A2E30-0x5A2E35, no ECX set), then takes the edge's destination `from->edges_begin[edge].to_province`, makes sure the CCurrentGameState exists (creating it if not - 0xDA8 bytes, CGameState::CGameState, vftable 0x15CF674), and walks that province's own template edges. For each neighbour whose controller is hostile to the unit's owner by the relation record at country +0xE28 (+0x20 set), it multiplies the cost by 3000/1000 once if the neighbour's **CProvince +0x300, unnamed** has a level above zero and once if **+0x304, unnamed** does - two specific buildings, which the province's building array at +0x310 would name. The loop stops once both multipliers have been applied, and is skipped entirely when the destination's template flag +0x22 is set. Returns `out` in EAX.
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature at all. Added: the same shape as the CPathFind::StepCost it overrides, __thiscall with five stack arguments and `ret 0x14`, answering `out` in EAX. Wrong if the forwarding at 0x5A2E30 is read as reordering the arguments.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5A2E00..0x5A3061. The five pushes at 0x5A2E30-0x5A2E34 are [ebp+0x18], [ebp+0x14], [ebp+0x10], [ebp+0xC], [ebp+8], no cleanup after the call. Its own uses agree with the base's roles: [ebp+0xC]+0x90 indexed by [ebp+0x10]*20 at 0x5A2E3A-0x5A2E43, [ebp+0x14]+0x2200 at 0x5A2F71, [ebp+0x18]+0x124/+0x128 at 0x5A2EC6, and `mov eax,[ebp+8]` at 0x5A3051 into the return. Shown wrong by a use of [ebp+8] as anything but the out pointer.

addresses.name: CParseContext::FreeMessages
addresses.comment:
Walks the message list freeing each node and its two strings, then clears first, last and count. The destructor calls it, and **nothing is logged on the way out** - which is why the mod's `common/` files never produce a line however many unknown keys they carry.

**It has no receiver anywhere.** ECX is dead at entry - the first instruction is `mov eax,[ebp+8]` - and dead at the call: CParseContext::~CParseContext (0x67A630) passes `this+4` on the stack having clobbered ECX in a `free` two instructions earlier, and `ret 4` cleans that one argument. So it is a free helper over the list head, not a member with its receiver in a register. The list itself **is** a CParseContext field: the destructor's argument is `this+4` and the site at 0x67C354 passes `[ebp+8]+4` of a CParseContext it is handed, so the head is messages_first/messages_last/messages_count at CParseContext +4/+8/+0xC. A node is two Hoi3CStrings, at +0 and +0x20, with the next pointer at +0x40 - not a LinkedListNode, which is why the parameter is typed for this list rather than as CList*.
addresses.revises: The recorded signature was `void __stdcall CParseContext::FreeMessages(void* list)` - a member name whose signature never mentions the class, which is what checkSignatures.py reported. The argument count and convention were right; what was missing is what the pointer is. Typing it CParseContextMessageList* says so and ties the name back to the class. Wrong if a fourth call site is found that passes something that is not a CParseContext's +4, or one that sets ECX to a receiver.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA7BAF0..0xA7BB5E, and all three callers from findRefs --callers: 0xA7A6DC-0xA7A6E0 (`add esi,4; push esi` with esi = ECX at the destructor's entry, and ECX last written by the `free` at 0xA7A6BE), 0xA7C34D-0xA7C354 (`mov edx,[ebp+8]; add edx,4; push edx`) and the two-instruction thunk at 0xA7BA20 (`push eax; call`). The node layout is read off the two string teardowns at +0x20/+0x30/+0x34 and +0x00/+0x10/+0x14 and the `mov edi,[esi+0x40]` that carries the walk. Shown wrong by a caller that pushes a CParseContext itself, or by finding the same list head reached from something that is not a CParseContext.

struct_fields.name: messages_first
struct_fields.comment: First node of the parse messages list; a node is two Hoi3CStrings at +0 and +0x20 with the next pointer at +0x40. CParseContext::FreeMessages is handed this field's address - the destructor passes `this+4` - and frees the chain.
struct_fields.evidence: The destructor at 0xA7A6DC does `add esi,4; push esi; call 0xA7BAF0` with esi = this, and 0xA7BAF0 reads [arg] as the head and clears [arg], [arg+4], [arg+8] at the end. Shown wrong by a use of CParseContext +4 as anything but a list head.

struct_fields.name: messages_last
struct_fields.comment: Last node of the parse messages list; cleared with the other two when the list is freed.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA7BB56 writes zero to [arg+4] where arg is CParseContext+4. Shown wrong by a reader of +8 that treats it as something other than a tail pointer.

struct_fields.name: messages_count
struct_fields.comment: How many messages are in the list; cleared when it is freed. Nothing reads it on the way out, which is why a file full of unknown keys is silent.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA7BB59 writes zero to [arg+8] where arg is CParseContext+4. Shown wrong by a reader of +0xC that treats it as a pointer.

struct_fields.name: kind
struct_fields.comment: What sort of edge this is. Only two values are tested here: CPathFind::MayStep and CPlannedPathFind::MayStep refuse an edge whose kind is 3 outright, and the helper at rva 0x1A2600 acts only on kind 1, which is a crossing through the province named at +8. The full set of values is not known.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [eax], 3` at 0x5A270C and 0x5A2D36, `cmp dword ptr [esi], 1` at 0x5A2610, in each case on the pointer the dispatch at 0x5A142C pushes as the fifth argument - which is `from->edges_begin + index*20`. Shown wrong by a site that reads +0 as anything but a small tag.

struct_fields.name: crossed_province
struct_fields.comment: The province a kind-1 edge crosses, as an index into CMap::provinces. The helper at rva 0x1A2600 refuses the step when that province's controller is hostile to the unit's owner, or when a foreign unit that is not retreating is standing in it - a strait or crossing that can be blocked.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x5A2622 `cmp dword ptr [esi+8], 0` guards it and 0x5A2649-0x5A264C does `mov eax,[esi+8]; mov eax,[provinces + eax*4]` on g_CMap's +0x2200 array, so it is a province id by construction. What is inferred is the name: shown wrong by a use of +8 that indexes something other than CMap::provinces.

slots_noted: Slots 0, 1 and 2 of all five tables are already recorded in project.json under the same names these entries use, so only slot 3 is added - repeating the others would write duplicate keys into the block. 0x1A12B0 and 0x67BAF0 are in no virtual table (vtable.py --holding).
